name: Building and curating the criteria library
summary: Mined repeat questions become person-approved categories, counted from the records and explorable in Neo4j.

steps.label: Mine repeat questions
steps.human:
An offline mining job, run apart from any decision, reads the published decision records and the Langfuse history of kernel runs, including failed, cancelled and never-published ones, and proposes the questions that keep coming back as candidate categories.

Published decision records bind the runtime DecisionRecord contract; candidate categories use the proposed mock-record design. The Langfuse trace read and the job's own invocation and candidate store are not defined.

steps.label: Approve a category
steps.human:
Decision point: you see each suggested category with its wordings and where they were seen, and accept it, change it or undo the grouping. Only your approval turns a candidate into a category record; the mining job and models never approve.

The person sees the candidate's mock-record fields. The approval question and answer for a category are not defined in a kernel run, and the design has no lifecycle stage between approval and staging.

criteria.question: Does the option name the unit a human approves (a category, a criterion, or a criterion's membership in a category) and give it a path like decision records have: staged in the run root, entered into Git only by a human-run publish command, and never created directly from Langfuse or from a mined candidate (ADR-060, ADR-058)?

Are category, decision_type and components top-level plain-YAML fields whose values come from declared vocabularies that validation enforces, with the category list itself a reviewed vocabulary (ADR-061 section 4)?
Can the ADR-062 projector read the store as one reviewed native kind with canonical ids, without changing how the existing Decision kind is read (its filename rule and pinned schema)?

Is category membership kept in one place outside the published decision records, so that merging, splitting or moving a criterion edits only category data, and retired ids stay resolvable through a recorded replaced-by link?
Does the format keep outcome and success statistics out of Git and expose only stable criterion or category ids that ADR-065's derived Neo4j aggregates can key on?

Does every stored criterion or category get a repository-unique, stable id with a declared kind under ADR-061's (repository_id, kind, id) key, with validation that rejects duplicate ids and dangling references, given that decision-local criterion ids already collide today?
Are usage counts (how many published decisions used a criterion or category) produced only by a generator from published records and checked for freshness like docs/decisions/index.json?

Do the existing readers of docs/decisions (validate and index in kernel/memory, the file precedent backend, the knowledge-map docs surface and the ADR-062 Decision projector) keep working without a change?
Can a later run find candidate criteria or categories by filter and by criterion wording, not only by a decision's question and title, without opening every file?
Can the format ship without a new config/paths.json surface or pre-commit hook, which would need an acceptance criterion with package_surface: true?

acceptance_scenarios.when: a person runs the offline mining job
acceptance_scenarios.then: repeat questions come back as candidate categories with proposed_by criteria_mining, approval_status proposed and mined_from sightings from both sources; a trace sighting is evidence for a proposal, never a member, and no decision run reads Langfuse or waits on the job

acceptance_scenarios.given: candidate categories, questions newly drafted for decisions and the published categories
acceptance_scenarios.when: groupings are suggested, by whichever method is chosen
acceptance_scenarios.then: each suggestion has one preferred wording, its other wordings and at most one broader category; no wording is suggested into two live categories, broader never leads back to its start, and nothing changes until a person accepts the suggestion

acceptance_scenarios.given: a candidate category proposed by criteria_mining
acceptance_scenarios.when: a person accepts it, after changing its wording or grouping if needed
acceptance_scenarios.then: it becomes approved with approved_by human:<name> and approved_at, and no path lets the mining job or a model approve it

acceptance_scenarios.when: a person rejects it or undoes its grouping
acceptance_scenarios.then: nothing is staged, no published category changes, and the candidate never becomes a record
its record is written to <run_root>/runs/<run_id>/staged/criterion_categories/<id>.yaml with lifecycle_stage staged and a stable cat- id, record_path stays null, and nothing is written into Git

acceptance_scenarios.when: a person runs the publish command and the change is reviewed and merged
acceptance_scenarios.then: the record is checked (every (decision id, criterion id) member names a published decision whose criteria carry that criterion in one of the category's wordings, and no wording sits in two live categories), written to docs/criteria/<id>.yaml with lifecycle_stage published, and no decision record changes

acceptance_scenarios.given: published categories whose members name published decisions
acceptance_scenarios.then: each category's usage_count equals the number of distinct decision ids among its members, a hand-edited count fails the freshness check, and the count never changes which categories are offered

acceptance_scenarios.given: published categories, the final outcomes of their member decisions and a configured Neo4j store
acceptance_scenarios.when: an added item triggers a rebuild
acceptance_scenarios.then: every aggregate row is rebuilt in full, keyed by category id and context, with decision_count equal to confirmed plus corrected plus abandoned plus pending and summing to the category's usage_count; category records carry no outcome statistics

acceptance_scenarios.given: no configured Neo4j learning store, or LEAFCUTTER_SELF_LEARNING=false
acceptance_scenarios.then: no outcome aggregates are built, usage counts are still generated, and decisions behave exactly as they do with the store

acceptance_scenarios.given: published category records with (decision id, criterion id) members and the published decisions they name
acceptance_scenarios.when: the knowledge sync builds a new generation from one commit
acceptance_scenarios.then: each published category becomes one node keyed by (repository_id, kind, id), each member pair links the decision, its criterion and the category, the generation is validated and published atomically, and Decision records are read exactly as before

acceptance_scenarios.given: a published category record with a member naming a criterion its decision does not carry

acceptance_scenarios.then: the build fails naming that record, the active generation stays untouched, and no file in Git is changed

provenance.note: Journey for building and curating the reusable criteria library (DK-500a, b, c, f and g) under decision dec-93c1c730463c1f3c, populated from leafcutter/criterion-categories. Created new because no existing flow covers CriterionCategory records; reuse inside a decision run extends leafcutter/decision-forming instead. Mining reads both published records and Langfuse traces as an offline job (user decision 2026-10-02). The grouping step is method-neutral while a kernel run decides the clustering method. The importer (DK-500g, in scope since the ADR-062 knowledge retrieval merged on main in PR #998) projects categories and membership through the native-type reader registry; the graph is a rebuildable view. No mockups exist, so no screens are wired. implements left empty for the business-analyst.

Merged origin/main (JSON contracts): io_contracts documented on all 14 nodes. Category records and aggregate rows use new illustrative_design schemas transcribed from leafcutter/criterion-categories, with stored samples cited from the dataset by pointer; published decision records bind the runtime DecisionRecord model with reconstructed projections. Undefined interfaces (Langfuse read, mining store, grouping output, approval, reject and curation answers, publish command, criteria index, Neo4j write, graph nodes and edges, category queries, import diagnostic) are explicit missing bindings; no-learning-store and change-in-record are not_applicable. Ids, order, implements and scenarios unchanged; readiness stays draft.
